source_evidence: Regular investing means that you put a set dollar amount or a set percentage of your income into your investment accounts.
answer: Regular investment contributions are amounts you put into an investment account on an ongoing basis. You can choose a set dollar amount or a percentage of your income. Keeping money invested over time can let compound growth build on both your contributions and the returns they earn. Starting earlier gives compounding more time to work, though investments involve risk and do not have a guaranteed rate of return.
